pr_title: Automated cherry pick of #129142: fix(dra): support multiple resource in PublishResources
pr_body:
Cherry pick of #129142 on release-1.32.

#129142: fix(dra): support multiple resource in PublishResources

Fixes: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/129122

For details on the cherry pick process, see the [cherry pick requests](https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-release/cherry-picks.md) page.

```release-note
This PR changes the signature of the `PublishResources` to accept a `resourceslice.DriverResources` parameter instead of a `Resources` parameter.
```

/assign @klueska 

This change only affects DRA drivers. We want this in a 1.32.x patch release to enable publishing multiple ResourceSlices by DRA drivers built for Kubernetes 1.32.

I'm impacted by this as I'm doing a DRA driver for networking, but I'm afraid this does not  match the current backport criteria , that it was also updated recently https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/8109 by @liggitt 

Since is a client only library exposed as a module, AFAIK clients can update the corresponding hash version until the new version is released `go get -u k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation@hash`, the specific commit was still not mirrored but I will confirm later once is published with my driver.

The other question is, thinking out loud here, if this is going to follow different semantics version that k/k then maybe it should be an independent repo and not a module from staging, but this is far of my knowledge of this library so I can be completely wrong here

> I'm impacted by this as I'm doing a DRA driver for networking, but I'm afraid this does not match the current backport criteria , that it was also updated recently https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/8109 by @liggitt

I agree that this normally wouldn't be considered necessary. But that PR leaves an escape hatch ("bolster your case by supplementing your PR") such that edge cases can be submitted for consideration. We have an issue (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129142) and @klueska from SIG Node suggested backporting. We can also ask in the WG Device Management meeting about the alternative (pinning to a hash) and whether that would be considered viable.

> The other question is, thinking out loud here, if this is going to follow different semantics version that k/k then maybe it should be an independent repo and not a module from staging, but this is far of my knowledge of this library so I can be completely wrong here

That would limit our ability to update the code in lockstep with API changes in k/k, like we did in the alpha->beta transition. It is used by the in-tree DRA test driver. The staging repo is the right compromise between "developed together with k/k" and "externally available".

> Since is a client only library exposed as a module, AFAIK clients can update the corresponding hash version until the new version is released `go get -u k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation@hash`, the specific commit was still not mirrored but I will confirm later once is published with my driver.

I agree with this. If you want access to this code, you can get it ahead of 1.33 by using `k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation@4361fe437fbafcf2e9cec648d590de43135b3b02` (the commit is already present at https://github.com/kubernetes/dynamic-resource-allocation/commit/4361fe437fbafcf2e9cec648d590de43135b3b02) ... I don't see why we would set a precedent of backporting changes like this to library modules minor versions.

issue_context.title: draplugin.PublishResources() only supports enumerating resources in a single slice
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

I wanted to publish multiple resource slices within the same pool, but there was no easy way to do this with the recommended helper library.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected the API to `draplugin.PublishResources()` to take a list of ResourceSlices, similar to the call to `resourceslice.Update()` that it wraps. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Examine the code here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin/draplugin.go#L427-L459
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/kubeletplugin/draplugin.go#L410

### Anything else we need to know?

/wg device-management

`v1.32.0`

None

Irrelevant

comments:
/triage accepted

This is an oversight. Ideally we should fix this quickly and backport to v1.32.1 for DRA drivers targeting 1.32.

Should we modify the original API interface or add a new one? 🤔 
like this: 
`PublishMultipleResources(ctx context.Context, resourcesList []Resources) error`

We can just change the existing Go API. It means that DRA drivers need to be updated when bumping their dependencies from v1.32.0 to v1.32.1, but that's okay: the k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation module has version v0.32.0 resp. v0.32.1, i.e. no API stability guarantee.

Got it, I'd like to try this.
/assign

> We can just change the existing Go API. It means that DRA drivers need to be updated when bumping their dependencies from v1.32.0 to v1.32.1, but that's okay: the k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation module has version v0.32.0 resp. v0.32.1, i.e. no API stability guarantee.

then why is it in staging if there is no guarantee between minors?

At least we should document it

Between 0.32.0 and 0.33.0? It's normal Go practice that there there is no API stability for 0.x releases. While we strive for more stability in staging repos, we also have always reserved the right to change APIs if needed. This one falls into that category.

Actually, it's even [documented explicitly already](https://github.com/kubernetes/dynamic-resource-allocation?tab=readme-ov-file#compatibility)! :smile:

Or did you mean between patch releases (major.minor.patch), i.e. 0.32.0 and 0.32.1?

While unusual, "no compatibility guarantees" also extends to patch releases.

> There are NO compatibility guarantees for this repository, yet. It is in direct support of Kubernetes, so branches will track Kubernetes and be compatible with that repo.

Kubernetes compatibility rules are much stricter as you can see in the backport rules, https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-release/cherry-picks.md

I don't see anything in that document about "don't break APIs".

I fully understand that this would be surprising and that it might not be important enough for a backport, but in this case forgetting to update that API in 1.32.0 is the bug that we want to fix.

Okay, let's not backport.

DRA driver authors who need this can pin their dependency to https://github.com/kubernetes/dynamic-resource-allocation/commit/4361fe437fbafcf2e9cec648d590de43135b3b02.

review_comments:
I'm not familiar with who calls this, or where this data goes, but do other things that interact with this map depend on the key being the node name?

What are the implications if something on node A populates this data with keys for node B?

No, the key can be arbitrary. It just needs to be unique among all pools published by the driver. If a driver doesn't ensure that, for example by using the name "my-pool" on all nodes, then the driver is broken and scheduling will not work, but that will only affect itself, not other drivers.
